text:
nina: quick follow-up on the windowed demotion idea from the RFC — trying to capture tradeoffs before we pick an impl. TL;DR: prefer soft-window scoring vs continuous LRU for small allocations.

sam: high level: windowed demotion buys us better locality for micro-batches but complicates prefetch heuristics. do we have data on short-lived vs medium-lived allocations?

nina: we sampled 24h on staging v2 (microbatch=4 workloads). ~68% of host-backed pages live < 120ms, another 20% between 120ms-5s, tail beyond that. so small window captures most churn.

taylor: ok that matches anecdotal. my worry: when we enforce a time-based window + recency score, eviction becomes non-monotonic with async offload. could produce thrash if prefetches mispredict.

maria: suggestion: tie the window to observed sequence-length distribution. shorter seq -> smaller window. easy toggle in config.

nina: +1. also thinking about a two-tier scoring: windowed hotness score (0..100) plus a fragmentation penalty. we need to avoid evicting tiny slabs that create lots of holes.

jordan: frag penalty sounds right. current alloc histogram shows small-slab holes account for ~12% of usable VRAM loss. if we evict aggressively we amplify that.

sam: can we pseudo-code the scoring? something like:
```
score = base_hotness(window) - frag_penalty(slab_size, hole_count) - prefetch_confidence_boost
```
then sort candidates by score.

taylor: watch out: sorting global candidate lists at eviction time is O(n log n) and will add jitter. maybe maintain approximate buckets (fast path) and slow exact sort only on pressure spikes.

maria: +1 on buckets. we already have an admission queue in the offload controller. reuse that for coarse-grained buckets (cold/warm/hot).

nina: ops question: how does this interact with host-pinned staging? if we demote too aggressively to host we may saturate PCIe and cause latency cliffs. ops-bot any telemetry?

ops-bot: pci_tx_util 9355551100..9355551220 shows sustained 60% during peak, spikes to 92% for 3s when staging churn > 1.2GB/s.

jordan: so we need a PCIe backpressure signal in the policy. if link util > 80% then increase demote threshold, or switch to async-batch demotes.

sam: implementation plan:
- 1) add windowed hotness metric (configurable ms)
- 2) add frag penalty metric that reads slab metadata (holes, free_frag_score)
- 3) reuse admission buckets for coarse scoring
- 4) add PCIe util soft-signal to demote policy (tie to scheduling)
- 5) telemetry: hotness distribution, slab fragmentation, pci_util, demote_rate per tenant

maria: timeline? feels like a mid-size refactor (allocator + offload controller + telemetry). estimate 2 sprints for PoC.

taylor: PoC should be behind a feature flag and a canary rollout (single pool) — we do need safety: auto-disable if latency regresses > 5th percentile by 30ms.

nina: agree. also add a deterministic reproducible test: small program that allocs pinned tensors with controlled lifetimes to exercise demote/fetch path. repo: eng-runtime/tests/demotion_repro.py

sam: one more open question: should the frag penalty be charged to the tenant that caused holes? that helps fairness but complicates cross-tenant reclaim.

jordan: prefer tenant-charged where possible. for shared slabs we can amortize by last-owner heuristics. document that in the RFC addendum.

maria: +emoji: :thumbsup: and i'll start a short PR for telemetry fields (hotness_bucket, frag_score, demote_backpressure).

nina: awesome. I'll draft the follow-up RFC addendum with scoring formula, bucket design, and canary plan. ping me if you'd like to coauthor.

sam: thanks all. filing a tracking issue: https://redwood.internal/issue/ENG-RUNTIME-1428

ops-bot: deploy-preview: offload-controller/feature/windowed-demote enabled on canary-pool-3 at 9355551245
